answer: Cash lasts [F7] before the covenant floor, not the [F5] a simple runway suggests; drawing the facility would extend that to [F9], so the board should choose now between drawing it and cutting burn.
exec_summary: Cash of [F1] at a burn of [F2] lasts [F5] in total.
The covenant floor of [F4] leaves [F6] usable, or [F7] of runway.
Adding the undrawn facility of [F3] lifts available liquidity to [F8], or [F9] of runway.
situation: A company funding its operating losses from cash, with an undrawn bank facility.
complication: The covenant floor shortens how long the cash really lasts.
key_question: How long does our cash last within the covenant, and how should we extend it?

titles.situation: Cash covers operations for now, but the covenant sets a floor.
titles.options: Three ways to extend the cash runway.
titles.recommendation: Keep the facility ready and cut burn first.
titles.roadmap: Decide at the board, then track runway monthly.
titles.kpis: Two measures show whether runway is under control.
titles.risks: The main risk is the bank changing the facility terms.

figures.label: Cash usable above the covenant floor

issue_tree.finding: The covenant floor cuts the real runway.
points: All cash lasts [F5] at the current burn.
Only [F6] sits above the floor of [F4], which lasts [F7].

hypotheses.text: The simple runway overstates how long cash lasts.

chart.title: The covenant floor shortens the cash runway.

issue_tree.finding: The facility adds runway but at a cost, and burn is the larger lever.
points: Drawing the facility of [F3] lifts usable liquidity to [F8].

hypotheses.text: The facility can be drawn when needed.
Burn can be cut without harming the business.

issue_tree.so_what: The board should decide on both levers while runway is still long.

chart.title: Usable liquidity rises once the facility is drawn.

options.name: Cut burn, keep the facility ready
options.description: Agree spending cuts now and keep the facility undrawn as a backstop.

options.name: Draw the facility now
options.description: Draw the full facility now to hold more cash.

options.name: Raise new equity
options.description: Start raising equity to fund operations.

recommendation.option: Cut burn, keep the facility ready
recommendation.rationale: Runway to the floor is [F7]; cutting burn extends it without interest cost, and the facility still adds liquidity up to [F8] if needed; the CFO decides.

actions: Bring the runway figures and the two levers to the board meeting.
Confirm with the bank that the facility can be drawn on current terms.
Track burn monthly against any cuts the board approves.
Refresh the runway with actual cash and update the board.

risks.risk: The bank changes the facility terms.
risks.mitigation: Confirm drawing conditions in writing before relying on it.

risks.risk: Spending cuts take longer to land than planned.
risks.mitigation: Phase the cuts and track them monthly.
